assumptions.name: Hidden state
assumptions.value: binary, each value with prior probability 1/2

assumptions.name: Private signal
assumptions.value: binary, equal to the hidden state with probability q, independent across agents given the state

assumptions.name: Observation networks
assumptions.value: complete history; last k predecessors (window-k), k in {2, 3}

assumptions.name: Visibility v
assumptions.value: 1, 0.5 (each action publicly recorded with probability v; the pattern is common knowledge)

assumptions.name: Sensitivity variations (EXP-003)
assumptions.value: V1: N = 50, coin ties; V2: N = 10, own ties; V3: N = 200, own ties

assumptions.name: Seeds and episodes
assumptions.value: master seeds 0 to 9, 1,000 episodes per seed and cell

assumptions.name: Common random numbers
assumptions.value: within a seed and cell, every rule sees the same state, signals and visibility pattern

assumptions.name: Rules
assumptions.value: independent (baseline): follow the own signal; Bayesian: exact posterior, all agents commonly known to be Bayesian; imitation: count observed actions as independent signals

assumptions.name: Smallest practically meaningful effect
assumptions.value: 0.01 on the proportion scale (stated in the sample-size rationale, not a decision rule)

assumptions.name: Multiplicity
assumptions.value: Holm adjustment at familywise 0.05 within each experiment or variation; intervals unadjusted

limitations: Synthetic agents only. The agents follow stylised rules. Results do not establish real human irrationality or rationality, and say nothing about any real platform or population.

Model scope. Binary state, binary symmetric signals, a single action per agent, homogeneous populations within an arm, and common knowledge of rules and network for the Bayesian agents. Heterogeneous preferences (where confounded learning can arise) are excluded.

Network family. Only the complete history and recent-window networks are studied, because exact Bayesian inference is tractable there. General random graphs are excluded; conclusions about "networks" are limited to these structures.
Imitation rule. Naive vote counting is one simple heuristic among many; other imitation rules can behave differently, as the degenerate pure-copy rule shows.
Metric choice. Episode accuracy averages over agents and depends on the horizon N; this is probed by EXP-003 but not eliminated.
Literature base. The M0 review is non-systematic and relies largely on abstracts.
Reproducibility versus validity. Exact reruns demonstrate computational reproducibility, not real-world validity.

Tie convention matters for magnitude. Coin-flip ties shrank every social-learning gain in the EXP-003 grid (by more than half in 16 of 24 contrasts) and removed Holm significance at q = 0.55, window-3, v = 1 (EXP-003). The EXP-002 magnitudes are specific to the own-signal tie rule.

Robustness only partly tested. EXP-003 covers q in {0.55, 0.70}; the robustness of the 24 EXP-002 contrasts at q in {0.60, 0.80} is untested by a confirmatory analysis. M4 update: the exploratory, post-hoc run EXP-004-R001 found all 72 comparisons at these q robust (CLM-010); this does not make them confirmatory.

Mean versus distribution. The primary estimand is a mean paired difference. Episode accuracy is bimodal under social learning, and wrong cascades are frequent (up to 0.87 of episodes in EXP-002), so a positive mean does not say that every group gains. No distributional estimand was preregistered. M4 update: exploratory analysis puts the share of episodes in which the social group ends below the baseline at 0.050 to 0.425 (CLM-011).

Imitation versus Bayesian not tested. Differences between the two social rules in the window networks (EXP-002) are exploratory; no planned test compares them directly. M4 update: exploratory paired intervals are in CLM-013 (no multiplicity control).

Practical size. Two Holm-significant EXP-002 contrasts (+0.0059 and +0.0091, q = 0.55, window-2, v = 0.5) are below the 0.01 effect the protocol calls the smallest practically meaningful (CLM-014); under coin ties 5 of 48 contrasts are below it.

Unverified literature detail. The protocols attribute coin-flip tie-breaking to BHW1992; this was not checked against the full text (publisher page inaccessible). The frozen protocols are not edited; reports and manuscript do not rely on the attribution. *Resolved at M6 (2026-11-25):* the full text (section II.A) states the coin-flip convention for the specific model; the general model of the paper lets indifferent individuals adopt.

Verification coverage of the window code. The exact oracle covers N <= 9 and the analytic anchor only the complete network with v = 1; a window-network error that appears only at larger N cannot be excluded, and it would move both social rules together.

Quantity versus structure not separable. In this grid the window networks have both less and differently placed information than the complete network; the design cannot attribute network differences to structure (EXP-004 Q4, CLM-015).
